visual_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 2 more clearly and accurately places the 30° launch vector and its horizontal/vertical components with correct formulas, while Lesson 1’s projectile diagram is generally correct but the component visualization is tiny/faint and appears to emphasize the vertical component when the prompt is asking for the horizontal speed.

interactivity.rationale: Lesson 1 includes a well-formed, wired fill-in gate with a real prompt, accepted answer, hint, and remediation path after a specific act, while Lesson 2 has no available gate specs or plan JSON and therefore no functioning checkpoints.

narration_quality.rationale: Lesson 1 is more naturally paced and structured into clear spoken beats with no raw notation defects, while Lesson 2 is a single dense run-on narration with a clipped/grammatically incomplete opening that makes the audio flow less polished.

sync.rationale: Lesson 1 has several cues that are timed near the narrated references despite some missing or early cues, whereas Lesson 2 provides no beat/timing data or visual cue triggers at all, making its synchronization unsupported and effectively worse on this dimension.

concept_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 2 presents the full correct calculation with explicit components, flight-time formula, and range multiplication, while Lesson 1 has a good conceptual sequence but its script leaves key equations and numerical steps mostly unstated, making the explanation less self-contained for a first-time learner.

polish.rationale: Lesson 2 has much larger, more legible text and a cleaner mid-lesson composition, while Lesson 1’s mid-lesson diagram is tiny, low-contrast, and pushed into the lower-left with excessive empty space, though Lesson 2 is hurt by visible browser/video UI and a weaker title slide.

aggregator.explanation: The six dimensions split 3-3, but the higher-confidence wins slightly favor Lesson 1. Lesson 1 was strongly preferred for interactivity, with a functioning fill-in checkpoint and remediation, and also won sync with supported timed cues; it also had a moderate narration-quality advantage. Lesson 2 was better for visual accuracy, concept accuracy, and polish, especially with clearer component diagrams, fuller calculations, and more legible layout. Overall, Lesson 1’s advantages in interactivity and synchronization carry slightly more weighted confidence than Lesson 2’s presentation and conceptual strengths.
